title: Crispy aloo tikki chaat, street style 🥔✨ #shorts
dish_fact: Aloo tikki began as a vegetarian kebab in Mughal royal kitchens and became North India's favourite street snack - the same crisp potato patty is served a dozen different ways from Delhi to Lucknow.

segments.moment_description: Cozy village morning: the young woman lifts a basket of earthy potatoes from the garden, brushing off the soil, soft golden sunlight and green leaves around her, Studio Ghibli anime screenshot, Hayao Miyazaki style, 2D hand-drawn animation cel, flat cel-shaded colors, visible ink linework
Steamed potatoes are peeled and mashed smooth in a big bowl by hand, then she mixes in chopped green chilli, grated ginger, fresh coriander, cumin and garam masala, a warm close-up of the spiced mash
Her palms scoop the mash and pat it into neat round patties, dusting each lightly with cornflour and smoothing the edges, a tidy row of raw tikkis lined up on a plate
The patties shallow-fry on a hot iron griddle in shimmering ghee, a deep golden-brown crust forming with tiny bubbles, a spatula flips one to reveal the crisp side, sizzling
A crisp tikki is set on a leaf plate and topped with dark tamarind chutney, bright green chutney and a spoon of whisked yogurt drizzling over it, glossy and colourful
A final shower of chaat masala, ruby pomegranate seeds, crunchy sev and coriander goes on top, then a fork breaks one tikki open to show the soft steaming potato inside - the irresistible reveal
